attempts.raw_response: The lodges and tents will be set among existing woodland and grassland, with landscaping designed to blend into the surrounding environment. Materials such as timber, green roofs, and natural stone will be used to minimise visual impact. The accommodation will be clustered in small groups, each with its own private outdoor space, and linked by winding footpaths. Christon emphasised that the aim was to create an immersive experience, allowing guests to feel as though they were sleeping within the animals' world. The development is expected to create around 30 new jobs and boost local tourism. Construction is scheduled to begin in early 2022, with the first guests welcomed later that year.

pair.human_continuation: "It'll be something that's never been seen before at any zoo in the world, so our visitors can wake up in the morning, open the curtains and look across the savannah and see the animals," Mr Christon said. There were some concerns about the development sitting in Cheshire's green belt, the Local Democracy Reporting Service wrote. Objector Les Smith told the planning committee there was "no justification" for the new accommodation, and that it was '"just about money", But Labour councillor Matt Bryan said the zoo had considered a "much larger" development but re-examined "how they can work sustainably with the animals they have got on the site, provide a new offer to our local economy, with a relatively modest amount of overnight units".
pair.prefix: Cheshire West and Chester Council has granted permission for the Grasslands development, which includes 28 "discreet" lodges and 14 "rigid tents". The zoo said it wanted the design to pay homage to animals' natural habitat. 'Total reorganisation' The zoo's chief operating officer Jamie Christon said it was a "major project" set to open in 2022, involving a "total reorganisation" of the western side of zoo. Nocturnal and early morning tours would also be offered for those staying overnight, he added.
